anemia.note: Symptoms are nonspecific; tuberculosis itself and nutritional or bleeding causes must also be considered.

thrombocytopenia.note: Bleeding symptoms or marked thrombocytopenia require prompt clinical assessment.

neutropenia.note: Fever with significant neutropenia can be clinically urgent.

monitoring.baseline: CBC including hemoglobin, white-cell differential and platelets before treatment.
monitoring.who_initial_schedule: Because of the anemia risk with linezolid, WHO guidance states Hb should be checked at least every 2 weeks for the first month, then monthly during linezolid exposure; CBC should be more frequent when clinically indicated or baseline Hb/neutrophils/platelets are low.
monitoring.timing_note: Myelosuppression is dose/exposure related and often appears during the first 1–3 months of linezolid exposure.

safety_rules: Never infer anemia, thrombocytopenia or neutropenia from symptoms alone; retrieve CBC results and clinical context.
Do not tell a patient to independently reduce, interrupt or restart linezolid.
If significant myelosuppression develops, retrieve current WHO/clinical guideline management pathway and route medication changes to the treating team.
Evaluate alternative causes of anemia, cytopenias and infection rather than automatically attributing every abnormal count to linezolid.
For fever plus known/severe neutropenia, escalate according to local urgent-care pathway.
For active or significant bleeding with thrombocytopenia, escalate promptly.
